reviews.review: This is a genuinely good game. Huge and detailed. The companions aren't the most compelling, and some aspects are a little repetitive, but for the most part, this is actually great.

I do not recommend this game. If you are in love with the trilogy, just don't play this one. 

So, here is the story: I bought it right after I finished the Mass Effect Legendary Edition - all three in a row. I had never played Mass Effect and I was stunned by how good it is even now. After that, I wanted to experience more of it. Of course, Andromeda was the game I chose. The worst happened: It started ruining my memories about Mass Effect. The more I played the worse it became.

Now, this abomination that uses the same words "Mass" and "Effect" has nothing to do with the perfect trilogy. They destroyed everything that was great about the series and added millennial ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Mass Effect was about the relationships, dialogues, decisions, and emotions.

Here in Andromeda, the dialogues are generic as hell and are somewhere between 5th and 7th grade level. Here is the example: I helped a guy save his team or the information they collected—I don't even remember because it was so generic. He says: "Thanks." My options to answer were: 1. "That's what friends do," 2. "Now we are friends?" 3. "You'd have done the same for a friend," 4. I don't remember. For me, that was the pinnacle of the game, and I remembered that dumb dialogue because it explains the whole game.

The graphics are better, sure, cannot argue. Some planets are beautiful, and actually, the places inside the monoliths look amazing. However, what happened to the characters? Whatever I did, my character looked like a 19-year-old intern. Other members of the team were weird, too. The Krogan was the only guy who was mature and whose dialogues inside the transport were fun to listen to. Female models all look like they have spinal issues. I'm not joking—you can check the images on the internet.

The gameplay itself as a shooter is indeed better than in the original trilogy. But, guys, let's be honest—it is still worse than in actual good shooters.

On one of the planets, they tried to recreate Aria. Disgusting. Very bad writing. I did not believe a single situation with her, and the dialogue options are better left unknown.

Just let me get this straight. I had a mission to basically save humanity. Why were all the dialogues and quests about "oh let's be friends"? There was no story, no drama at all. One of the decisions led to me losing one of my team members, and I had to choose which one. I chose without any hesitation because I had zero emotional connection to any of them.

My problem with this game is that they prentended it is a Mass Effect. They knew the expectations, right? They failed. 

So, in the end, you may think that I am just a hater, but if you loved the trilogy, just remember it as it is. Don't ruin your memories with this.
I don't care what anyone says, Andromeda is a damn good time. Best combat in the series by far, good crafting system, and I appreciate the "lost in space vibe Bioware went for.
